_comment: Shared OTA timing contract, consumed by BOTH app test suites:
Each suite asserts its own platform's table equals this file, so changing
one platform's numbers without the other fails that platform's build.
This is APP BEHAVIOUR, not a wire format — nothing here is transmitted, so
it lives outside fixtures/wire/ (which the freshness gtest owns) alongside
crossesRelay marks a stage whose completion depends on the FC answering
over the OC relay. Those MUST be longer on the FC path; the rest are local
phone-to-OC events and MUST be identical. A stage that crosses the relay
with fc == local is the bug found on the bench 2026-07-28: finish sat at a
flat 15 s on both platforms while a live 591.7 kB FC flash was still
running, so the app declared failure on a transfer that then succeeded.

stages.name: begin
stages.why: FC erases its OTA slot before it can answer ready

stages.name: finish
stages.why: FC drains the I2S ring, writes the tail, SHA-256s the image and sets the boot partition

stages.name: fwPublish
stages.why: FC reboots, then the OC has to re-query its identity before the new version reaches the app

stages.name: disconnect
stages.why: local BLE link drop; the relay is not involved

stages.name: reconnect
stages.why: phone re-establishes its own link to the OC; already generous

_fcRelayPumpComment: Ceiling on the chunk pump for FC-relay OTAs ONLY; a local OC OTA stays
uncapped (it writes straight to flash, no relay, and runs happily at
#627: on the relay path the OC re-sends each chunk to the FC over I2S. Pump
faster than it can drain and the 16-deep feed queue fills, receive buffers
stop being retired, NimBLE's ACL mbuf pool exhausts and the BLE link wedges
— thousands of 'ACL buf alloc failed' / 'MBUF alloc stuck', then the OC
simply stops receiving (bench 2026-07-28: enq frozen at 3418 for 135 s).
The FC then sees a hole and, being forward-only, discards everything after.
Bench-measured on the same board and image: iOS pumps 11.4 kB/s and the
relay works; Android pumps ~68 kB/s and it fails. iOS was never CORRECT
here, just slow enough to stay under an unstated limit. 12000 keeps the
proven-good rate for both platforms and makes it explicit — on iOS this is
very nearly a no-op, on Android it is the fix.
A 591.7 kB FC image therefore takes ~50 s to upload, which is why the FC
finish window is 60 s (see the finish stage above).
